ImageDescription.value: The Currier & Ives lithograph shows people fleeing across the Randolph Street Bridge. Thousands of people literally ran for their lives before the flames, unleashing remarkable scenes of terror and dislocation. "The whole earth, or all we saw of it, was a lurid yellowish red," wrote one survivor. "Everywhere dust, smoke, flames, heat, thunder of falling walls, crackle of fire, hissing of water, panting of engines, shouts, braying of trumpets, roar of wind, confusion, and uproar."

The Chicago River is the south border of the Near North Side and Streeterville and the north border of the New Eastside (viewed from Lake Shore Drive with Trump International Hotel and Tower at the jog in the river at the center.
This 6-part composite panorama shows the optical center of the main branch of the Chicago River looking west (upstream) as seen from the upper vehicle deck of the Lake Shore Drive Bridge.
